section: data: c4, and why filtering beats volume
text: Data: C4, and why filtering beats volume §2.2, §3.4, Tables 8 and 9 C4 is about 750 GB of English (745 GB in Table 8 ) from one month of Common Crawl (April 2019), cleaned with blunt heuristics ( §2.2 ): keep only lines ending in terminal punctuation and with at least 5 words; drop pages with fewer than 3 sentences; drop pages with a word from the "List of Dirty, Naughty, Obscene or Otherwise Bad Words", with "lorem ipsum", or with a curly bracket (a cheap code detector); drop lines mentioning Javascript or policy boilerplate ("terms of use", "cookie policy" and similar); strip Wikipedia citation markers; keep one copy of any repeated three-sentence span; keep pages langdetect calls English with probability at least 0.99. without those filters (language detection kept) the corpus is 6.1 TB, 8.2 times larger.
